title: Small-chunk localized evaluation is a weak exponential
statement:
Use combinatorial simplicial model categories and projective enriched diagrams of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], and Dwyer--Kan homotopy theory and enriched localization of [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus]. Fix universes, a combinatorial simplicial model category $\mathcal M$, and small simplicial categories $I,J$. A chunk $U\subseteq\mathcal M$ means a full simplicial subcategory with these closure properties, with choices functorial by enriched functors: every finite fan $X\to Y_i$ in $U$ has a factorization $X\to Z\to\prod_iY_i$ as a trivial cofibration followed by a fibration with $Z\in U$, and every finite cofan $Y_i\to X$ has a factorization $\coprod_iY_i\to Z\to X$ as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration with $Z\in U$; empty families are included. For a small simplicial category $I$, $U^I$ denotes the full enriched subcategory of $\mathcal M^I$ of diagrams valued in $U$. An $I$-chunk means that $U$ is a chunk and $U^I$ is a chunk in the projective model structure.

Let $U$ be a small chunk which is an $I$-chunk, and put $U_f^I=U^I\cap(\mathcal M^I)^f$, $E_U(I)=U_f^I[W_I^{-1}]$, and $X_U=U^f[W_U^{-1}]$, where the distinguished arrows are the model weak equivalences. For an enriched functor $v:J\to I$, put
$$P_U(I,J)=(U_f^I\times J)[V^{-1}],\qquad V=\{(w,1_j):w\in W_I,\ j\in\operatorname{Ob}J\}.$$
Projection to the two factors gives a canonical Dwyer--Kan equivalence
$$P_U(I,J)\longrightarrow E_U(I)\times J,$$
and the latter ordinary product represents the homotopy product. Evaluation $(F,j)\mapsto F(vj)$ induces an enriched map $P_U(I,J)\to X_U$. These diagrams are functorial under restriction in $I$, change of $J$, and full inclusions of chunks whenever the indicated chunks exist.

If $I$ is cofibrant in the Dwyer--Kan model structure and $v=1_I$, this evaluation exhibits $E_U(I)$ as a weak exponential of $X_U$ by $I$. Explicitly the evaluation span induces, for every small simplicial category $T$, a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(T,E_U(I))\ \cong\ \operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(T\times^h I,X_U),$$
natural in $T$, where $h\mathrm{sCat}$ is the ordinary homotopy category of the Dwyer--Kan model structure and $\times^h$ denotes its homotopy product. The evaluation is the one induced from the actual enriched mapping sets, rather than from a coherent nerve.

source.place: Definition A.3.4.1 and Notation A.3.4.9 for the inline chunk and I-chunk definitions; Corollary A.3.4.14, printed p.890; Lemma A.3.5.14, printed p.896; Lemma A.3.6.17 and the evaluation spans in the proof of Proposition A.3.6.16, printed pp.904-905, specialized to simplicial sets. Read online on 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: Put $A=U_f^I$. Its objects are objectwise fibrant, because projective fibrations are objectwise [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. On mapping simplicial sets define evaluation at $v$ by sending $(\alpha,u)$, with $\alpha:F\to G$ and $u:j\to k$ of the same simplicial degree, to $G(vu)\alpha_{vj}=\alpha_{vk}F(vu)$. The equality is enriched naturality. The enriched unit and composition equations show that this defines a simplicial functor $A\times J\to U^f$. A distinguished $(w,1_j)$ maps to $w_{vj}$, a model weak equivalence. Composing with $U^f\to X_U$ therefore inverts all of $V$, and the enriched localization construction gives the asserted map $P_U(I,J)\to X_U$. The same argument applied to the two projections defines the left map to $E_U(I)\times J$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.3.6.16, evaluation spans, printed pp.904-905.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-product-parameter] with $C=A$, $D=J$, $W=W_I$. Smallness holds and its marked arrows are exactly $V$. Its comparison is Step 1's left map, so that map is a DK equivalence. Here is also the ordinary-product comparison, including non-Kan factors. Write $R=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$. By [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products], $R$ preserves finite products, $RX$ is Kan, and $j_X:X\to RX$ is a natural weak equivalence. Naturality and two-out-of-three imply $Rf$ is weak whenever $f$ is. For a weak $f:X\to Y$, the map $Rf\times1_{RZ}$ is the pullback of $Rf$ along $RY\times RZ\to RY$; this projection is a Kan fibration since $RZ$ is Kan. Right properness [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] makes this pullback weak. Under the product comparison $j_X\times j_Z$ equals $j_{X\times Z}$, and likewise for $Y$, so two-out-of-three makes $f\times1_Z$ weak. Thus products preserve local weak equivalences of simplicial categories; their component categories are the products of the component categories (apply $R$ to the mapping sets), so they preserve DK equivalences. Replace both categories by fibrant ones. The product of these fibrant replacements computes their derived product: on a discrete pair of objects fibrant replacement is coordinatewise. The original product maps to it by a DK equivalence. Hence the ordinary product represents the homotopy product, in the derived-limit convention of [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus].

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.14; first verification in the proof of Proposition A.3.6.16, printed pp.896,905.

proof.text: Restriction $r^*:U_f^I\to U_f^{I'}$ along $r:I'\to I$ preserves fibrant objects and weak equivalences because they are objectwise. A change $s:J'\to J$ changes the evaluation index to $vs$, while a commuting square $rv'=vs$ gives $(r^*F)(v'j')=F(vsj')$. Full inclusions $U\subseteq U'$ preserve the same fibrant diagrams and distinguished arrows. The identical equations on enriched maps show that evaluation and both projections commute with these operations. Functoriality of enriched localization supplies the stated functorial diagrams, whenever the specified chunks exist. This argument uses no preservation of projectively cofibrant diagrams by restriction.

source.place: Evaluation spans in the proof of Proposition A.3.6.16, printed p.904.

proof.text: For the exponential assertion assume $I$ cofibrant and set $B=(U^I)^{cf}$ and $K=U^{cf}$. Here $cf$ for $B$ refers to the projective model structure. Apply [lem-coef-chunk-bifibrant-localization] first to the chunk $U$ in $\mathcal M$, then to the chunk $U^I$ in the combinatorial simplicial model category $\mathcal M^I$. These are precisely the two chunk assumptions on $U$. It gives Dwyer--Kan equivalences $\eta:K\to X_U$ and $\theta:B\to E_U(I)$. Evaluation preserves bifibrancy by [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], so it gives $e:B\times I\to K$. By Step 2's product argument the products $B\times I$ and $E_U(I)\times I$ are homotopy products and $\theta\times1_I$ is a DK equivalence. The inclusion $B\times I\to U_f^I\times I$ followed by localization gives $k:B\times I\to P_U(I,I)$. Its composite with the left map is $\theta\times1_I$ and its composite with evaluation is $\eta e$, by the formulas in Step 1. Thus the localized evaluation span agrees in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ with the actual enriched evaluation $e$ under these equivalences.

source.place: Lemma A.3.6.17 and the final comparison of evaluation spans in the proof of Proposition A.3.6.16, printed pp.904-905.

proof.text:
First compute unrestricted evaluation. Put $\widehat B=(\mathcal M^I)^{cf}$ and $\widehat K=\mathcal M^{cf}$. For every small $T$, [lem-coef-simplicial-diagram-equivalence-classes], applied to the combinatorial projective model $\mathcal M^I$ and then to $\mathcal M$, gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(T,\widehat B)\cong\pi_0((\mathcal M^I)^T)\cong\pi_0(\mathcal M^{I\times T})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I\times T,\widehat K).$$
The middle isomorphism curries $F:T\to\mathcal M^I$ into $(i,t)\mapsto F(t)(i)$, with action in the two variables commuting by enriched naturality. It preserves and reflects weak equivalences, since both classes are objectwise at $(i,t)$. The two projective structures have the same objectwise fibrations and weak equivalences, so also the same cofibrations by their lifting characterization. Evaluation on a bifibrant representative is therefore the map giving this bijection; the mapping-end description of enriched diagrams identifies its full simplicial action with Step 1's formula. Both class bijections are natural, hence so is this bijection. No cofibrancy of $I\times T$ is required for the unrestricted class theorem.

source.place: Proposition A.3.4.13 and its proof using Proposition A.3.4.12, printed p.890.

proof.text: The inclusions $b:B\hookrightarrow\widehat B$ and $a:K\hookrightarrow\widehat K$ are fully faithful on mapping simplicial sets: they are full enriched subcategories. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-fully-faithful-homotopy-image] with sources $T$ and $I\times T$, respectively. It says that both induced maps on Hom sets are injective, and their images consist exactly of maps whose object values, up to isomorphism in the corresponding $\pi_0$ category, belong to the respective subcategory. Under Step 5's bijection, an element in the image of $b_*$ has every row $I\to\widehat K$ represented by an object of $B$. Every such row takes values in $K$, by preservation of bifibrancy under evaluation. Thus its image is in the image of $a_*$.

source.place: Corollary A.3.4.11 and the proof of Corollary A.3.4.14, printed pp.889-890.

proof.text: Conversely let $\alpha:I\times T\to\widehat K$ denote a derived morphism in the image of $a_*$, and let $\beta:T\to\widehat B$ be its inverse image under Step 5. Fix an object $t$ of $T$. Naturality under $\{t\}\to T$ says that the object class $\beta(t)$ corresponds to the row $\alpha_t:I\to\widehat K$. Every object of this row is in the essential image of $K$. The image criterion of [lem-coef-simplicial-fully-faithful-homotopy-image], now with source $I$, gives a class $\gamma_t:I\to K$ mapping to $\alpha_t$. Since $I$ is cofibrant and $U$ is an $I$-chunk, the restricted bijection of [lem-coef-simplicial-diagram-equivalence-classes] represents $\gamma_t$ by a diagram in $U^I$. Cofibrant and fibrant replacement within $U^I$ (the empty-family chunk factorizations) gives an object $F_t\in B$. Compatibility of the restricted and unrestricted bijections says that $\beta|_{\{t\}}$ equals the derived map selecting $F_t$. The image criterion for $b$ with source $\{t\}$ therefore puts $\beta(t)$ in the essential image of $\pi_0b$. Applying that criterion with source $T$ puts $\beta$ in the image of $b_*$. The separate choices $F_t$ establish this image condition only; that criterion supplies the coherent derived map into $B$, so no incoherent assembly of chosen rows is assumed.

source.place: Corollary A.3.4.14 via Corollary A.3.4.11 and the restricted class bijection, printed p.890.

proof.text:
Steps 6-7 identify exactly the two image subsets of the unrestricted bijection in Step 5. Its restriction is consequently a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(T,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I\times T,K).$$
It is induced by $e$, because the square with the two injective inclusion maps commutes with evaluation, and it is natural in $T$, because the unrestricted bijection and the two inclusions are natural. Step 2 identifies ordinary products with homotopy products; interchange of factors identifies $I\times T$ with $T\times^h I$. Step 4's isomorphisms $[B]\cong[E_U(I)]$ and $[K]\cong[X_U]$ transfer this natural bijection to exactly the one asserted in the item. The equality of the two evaluation composites in Step 4 shows it is induced by the displayed localized evaluation span. Every evaluation used here was defined on actual enriched mapping simplicial sets in Step 1; no coherent-nerve evaluation was substituted.

source.place: Final paragraph of the proof of Proposition A.3.6.16, printed p.905.
